title: One Way
label: Planet Mu

type.basis: Album on an electronic label; documents grime instrumentals reaching a wider electronic audience.

sound.text: Planet Mu: grime fused with hip hop, electro and drum and bass, with 'menacing bass' and 'spacey production'.
Igloo (Jan 2005): largely instrumental, 'trudging and dark'; 'Bang Bang Boy' is hard and noisy, unlike typical grime minimalism.
Daily Lobo (Jan 2005): brooding Wu-Tang strings and instrumentals with a dub-reggae-like effect; 'Bang Bang Boy' has gun samples over a 'wobbly dred bass'.
sound.pub: Jan 2005 (Daily Lobo, Jonny Pelham; date from URL)

context.text: Igloo calls it one of the first full-length grime albums to get wide attention outside the UK, and Planet Mu's first major grime release.
Wikipedia lists Mark One as a past member of Manchester's Virus Syndicate, who often supplied the vocals on his solo recordings, including One Way.
Mark One was a former drum and bass DJ (Daily Lobo).

uncertainty: Mark One's own home city was not confirmed (Virus Syndicate are from Manchester). The release date comes from Planet Mu's own listing. Format comes from the Igloo page title.
tracklist: Mostly instrumental, with three tracks featuring Virus Syndicate MCs (JSD on 'Stand Up', MC Goldfinger on 'Ready for It', Nika D on 'Contagious Rhymin''). Other tracks named: 'Bang Bang Boy', 'Call Back', 'Blow', 'Bring the Law'.
